frequency_question: How often do central banks implement incremental reserve ratio requirements within a specific multi-month operational window following observable interbank liquidity surges?
membership_rule: Includes any formal announcement and implementation of secondary, incremental, or ad-hoc reserve requirements specifically targeted at absorbing excess banking system liquidity by major emerging market central banks. Excludes standard annual or routine structural changes to baseline reserve requirement ratios.

cases.name: RBI iCRR equivalent (Incremental CRR historical uses)
Central Bank of Turkey liquidity reserve measure

provenance_note: claims 18 cases from only 5 named (3.6x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 5 named historical episodes capturing ad-hoc liquidity management tool deployments out of approximately 18 distinct systemic liquidity overhang cycles.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller frontier market central banks where reporting of ad-hoc liquidity measures is less systematically archived.
skeleton: Major liquidity absorption episodes across systemically important emerging markets experiencing sudden capital inflows or currency intervention side-effects over 25 years, categorized by whether advance liquidity overhang precursor signals were visible.
multiplier: 5 observed ad-hoc liquidity-absorption instrument implementations across 18 major liquidity surge cycles where precursor signals were monitored.
validity_reason: Central bank operational toolkits for liquidity management evolve slowly over decades, keeping structural base rates stable.
